source_text: Agite igitur, carissimi, et nos angelicam consectantes laudem, debitum pro viribus grati persolvamus, dicentes: Ave ac gaude, gratia plena, Dominus tecum. Tuum enim vere est avere, atque gaudere: quoniam tecum divina gratia, ut novit, habitationem elegit: cum ancilla, Rex gloriae: cum speciosa, speciosus forma prae filiis hominum: cum impolluta, qui sanctificat universa. Tecum Deus, et ex te Deus, ac perfectus homo, in quo omnis plenitudo divinitatis inhabitat.
thought_title: Joining the angel's greeting to Mary
orientation: The preacher now exhorts the congregation to take up Gabriel's greeting to Mary after recounting that the Lord is with her.
pass_a_gloss: Come now therefore, dearest ones, and we pursuing angelic praise, let us as grateful persons pay the debt according to our strengths, saying: Hail and rejoice, full of grace, the Lord with you. For truly it is yours to be hailed and to rejoice: since with you divine grace, as it knew, chose dwelling: with a slave-girl, the King of glory: with a beautiful one, the beautiful in form beyond the sons of men: with an undefiled one, he who sanctifies all things. With you God, and from you God, and perfect man, in whom all fullness of divinity dwells.

lemmas.gloss: to be hailed, to be greeted with Ave

choices.why: Agite is plural imperative exhortation, not narrative past; carissimi is vocative address to hearers.
Locked glossary rendering for the angel's greeting; keeps the nominal phrase rather than interpreting favor.

choices.english: to be hailed and to rejoice
choices.why: Keeps the Ave/avere wordplay and the distinct infinitive forces dependent on Tuum est, with gaudere as joy per glossary sense.

choices.english: beautiful in form beyond the sons of men
choices.why: Literal predicate phrase matching the psalm wording; prae is comparison beyond, not simple among.

bible_refs.note: Ave ac gaude, gratia plena, Dominus tecum
speciosus forma prae filiis hominum; Vulgate Psalm 44:3, Septuagint Psalm 44:3
in quo omnis plenitudo divinitatis inhabitat

pass_b_english: Come now therefore, dearest ones, and let us follow the angels in their praise. As grateful people, let us pay what we owe with all our strength, saying: "Hail and rejoice, full of grace, the Lord is with you" (Luke 1:28).

For to be hailed and to rejoice is truly yours, because divine grace has chosen to dwell with you, as it knows: with a maidservant is the King of glory; with the beautiful one is he who is beautiful in form beyond the sons of men (Psalms 45:2); with the undefiled one is he who sanctifies all things. God is with you, and God is from you, and perfect man, in whom all the fullness of deity dwells (Colossians 2:9).
